svg.title: A scraper does not throw. It returns None.
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a web page with a price cell highlighted beside two selectors - a brittle chain of positional child selectors and a generated class name struck through in red, and a resilient selector anchored to the Price label ticked in green; the central failure mode where a missing element returns None rather than raising and fills a warehouse column with NULLs with no exception and no log line; the fix as one guard line that raises at the extraction boundary so a CI job goes red on the pull request; and measured parse times of 2.72 seconds for BeautifulSoup with html.parser, 2.25 with lxml, and 0.159 seconds for direct lxml XPath.
svg.text: A scraper does not throw. It returns None.
one redesign and this is gone. The class name is generated.
anchors to MEANING, not to position
and here is how a scraper actually breaks
no exception. No log line. The
the fix is one line, at the boundary
if el is None: raise ExtractionError('price missing')
now it fails LOUDLY, at 09:14, on the pull request
instead of silently, in the warehouse, three weeks later
and the cost you were not measuring
the parser was never the bottleneck.
...and read the Terms too. This is not only a technical
